# Shared Goodix 5120 protocol reference

`protocol.ini` is an independent test oracle for the Go probe/helpers and C driver/helpers.
It is never generated from a production payload builder or used by a shipped command.
Go embeds it through `internal/testfixtures`; shared FDT integration tests also live there to keep
`internal/proto` and its tests standard-library-only. C uses GLib's `GKeyFile`, with its source path
set by the standalone Meson build. Both loaders fail on missing records, duplicates,
unknown fields, malformed hex/numbers, and incomplete inventories. No capture file is required.

## Provenance

- `init.00`–`init.13`, `health`, and `loop.*`: the health/capture catalogue and all 14 commands in [the documented init sequence](../../../docs/protocol.md#init-sequence),
  including both resets and MCU-state reads. The host timestamp is the reference's fixed `55 a2 52 00 00`.
- `init.10`: all 224 config bytes copied from [the recovered config](../../../docs/protocol.md#the-224-byte-0x90-config--recovered-observed-2026-09-20),
  rather than either implementation's array or a checksum-only assertion.
- Firmware, reset/chip/status/header bytes and response modes follow the same protocol evidence.
  Firmware uses the supported unterminated form; existing C regressions also test one trailing NUL.
- PSK hash and OTP bytes are **synthetic**: SHA-256 of `e4-psk-hash/0` and consecutive
  `a6-otp/<counter>` labels. MCU-state bodies retain the reference replay's example fields;
  their counters and unrelated flags are opaque. They do not represent calibration support.
- `arm.*`, `event.*`, and `pair.observed-*` consolidate the previously committed literal
  FDT vectors from Go and C tests. The seven observed pairs came from the documented vendor
  capture; `pair.run22-*` and the final lift retain the owner-reported Run 22 vectors.
  Boundary, baseline and attach-margin vectors have hand-calculated expected thresholds.
- `image` is a **synthetic** pattern. `12 34 56 78 9a bc` decodes to twelve-bit samples
  `234 781 c56 9ab`, then grayscale `23 78 c5 9a`. Repeat 1280 times for all 5120 samples.
  `aa` header bytes and `bb` trailer bytes expose incorrect trimming. These are not fingerprints.

No recovered key, device PSK hash, OTP contents, firmware blob, or biometric capture belongs here.
TLS handshake bytes remain generated by the existing synthetic OpenSSL client.

## Format and maintenance

INI sections preserve init order. Hex values are contiguous; command fields contain one byte.
Nonnegative numbers are decimal, bounded to 65535; numeric lists end with semicolons.
Reply modes are `none`, `ack`, `data`, `ack-data`, `tls`, or `ack-tls`; ACK status is `01`.
`secret=1` identifies PSK-hash/OTP replies. Event kinds are unknown/down/up/manual/base-invalid
(`0`–`4`). Arm timestamps are numeric inputs with literal little-endian payload expectations.

Each section requires exactly the fields consumed by its tests. Adding vectors requires updating
both loader inventories; this prevents an empty or truncated corpus silently passing.
Expected bytes must come from documented evidence or an independent calculation. Do not add an
update-golden command that obtains expectations from the implementation being tested.

Run `go test ./cmd/goodix-probe ./internal/proto ./internal/image ./internal/testfixtures` and
`meson test -C /tmp/goodix-build-c --print-errorlogs` after changing this reference. A passing
fixture suite establishes offline parity, not hardware recovery or authentication quality.
